int32.platform: linux/386 under QEMU user-mode emulation on linux/arm64

reference_commands: docker run --rm --network none -v tests/semantics/w10-ops:/w:ro IMAGE php -n /w/matrix.php | gzip -9 -n > internal/runtime/testdata/php8512-ops-WIDTH.json.gz

docker run --rm -i --network none -v tests/semantics/w10-ops:/w:ro IMAGE php -n /w/strings.php < internal/runtime/testdata/php8512-numeric-strings.txt | gzip -9 -n > internal/runtime/testdata/php8512-numeric-strings-WIDTH.jsonl.gz

result.fuzz: FuzzNumericString: 60 s, about 11.9 million executions, no failure after the 32-bit wrap fix

comparison: Each case compares the exact result encoding (float bits, string bytes, array keys and values), the thrown class and message, and every diagnostic level and message in order. NaN results compare as NaN regardless of sign and payload, which come from the host CPU and libm and are visible to PHP only through pack().
limitations: The 32-bit ** results with non-trivial floats differ from the emulated i386 reference by up to 64 ULP. QEMU computes x87 transcendental instructions less precisely than hardware, so these reference values are not a trustworthy oracle; the semantics-ops workflow regenerates both references natively on x86-64 and requires exact matches.
PHP 8.5.12 only; no other release has a profile or reference run.
Objects, resources, increment and decrement, compound assignment, intdiv, fmod, and string functions are not modeled.
pow uses 256-bit big.Float arithmetic for correct rounding, which is slower than math.Pow; performance work is not done.
